CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  NOVEMBER  11, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order  at
  6:42 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager  Rob Houston,  City
  Attorney  Rail  F. Salinas

1
PRESENTATIONS-  CITY'S

BUDGET/FISCALFUTURES  The City  Council  unanimously  received  and filed  a presentation  on the
  City's  Budget  and Fiscal  Future  by motion  of Vice Mayor  Barron  and
  seconded  by Council  Member  Hurtado.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios,  yes; Vice Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,
  yes.

RECESS  The City  Council  recessed  at 9:03 p.m.,  and reconvened  at 9:11 p.m.,  with
  all Members  of Council  present.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE-NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  - EMAIL  Mario  Dominguez  stated that South  Gate lacks bike friendly  infrastructure
  compared  to nearby  cities  and encouraged  the city to pursue  grants to
  develop  a bike trail.  He also requested  updates  on the fiber  optic  project
  timeline  and expected  completion  date for the Frontage  Road East Re-
  pavement  Project.

CONT'D  Carol Averell,  Housing  Manager  stated the Community  Development
  added on the city's  website  food  bank resources.

  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  stated that the recent
  legislation  related  to the requirement  to provide  broadcast  or call-in

  features  to the City  Council  Meetings  is being  researched  by city staff.
  Vendors were brought in to look at options the city has. One of the options
  being looked at is going to allow for a call-in feature. This is an unfunded
  mandate.

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  wished  everyone  a happy
  Veterans  Day.

  Manny  Arana,  Chief  of Police,  reminded  everyone  that on Saturday,
  November  15, 2025,  from  10:00  a.m. to 3:00 p.m.,  is the Family  Day at
  the Park at South  Gate Park.

  Rob Houston,  City  Manager,  clarified  why the Finance  Director  is talking

  about IT. Mr. Fausto  oversights  is both Finance  and IT.

  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney,  had nothing  to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City  Treasurer,  stated that outside  the Legacy  Complex

  the schools  are creating  a public  safety issue on Legacy  Lane and Tweedy.
  He has provided  the information  to City  Manager  and Chief  of Police.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  stated that Rotary  will  be serving  Thanksgiving

  dinner  to needy  families  in the community.  She may be reached  for tickets.

  Council  Member  Avalos  expressed  appreciation  and gratitude  to veterans

  for their  service,  noting  that military  service  can have a lasting  impact  on

  individuals.  She emphasized  the importance  of showing  returning  service

  members  patience,  kindness  and understanding.  While  recognizing  that

  although  veterans  may return  changed,  they remain  the same individuals
  deserving  of respect,  particularly  in light  of the freedoms  their  service
  helps protect.

  Council  MemberAvalos  also reported  attending  the State of the City
  event,  describing  it as informative  and expressing  appreciation  for the

  presentations  by city leadership  and the mayor.  Additionally,  she noted
  that the Southeast  Water  Coalition  meeting  was scheduled  but

  subsequently  canceled  and aru"iounced  that a Vector  Control  meeting  is

  scheduled  to take place on Thursday.

CONT'D  Council  Member  Hurtado  thanked  the veterans  for their  service.  He
  mentioned  that on Tuesday,  November  25'h from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.,
  or while  supplies  last, Assemblymember  Jose Luis  Solache,  Jr., is having  a
  turkey  giveaway  for residents  of Huntington  Park, Maywood,  Walnut
  Park, South  Gate, Lynwood,  Paramount,  Bellflower,  and Lakewood  at the
  South Gate Park.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated the JAA  is purchasing  100 turkeys  from
  Walmart.  They  are also purchasing  40 additional  turkeys  thanks  to the
  $400 donation  from  Liz Ruiz.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  the veterans  for their  service.  He too
  attended  the State of the City.

  Steve Costely,  Director  of Parks & Recreation,  stated having  a great
  veteran's  event last Saturday.  There was also a Special  Olympic  event.  He
  stated Assemblymember  Solache  will  be giving  away  one thousand
  turkeys  and one thousand  pumpkin  pies. He reminded  everyone  of the
  Pageant  of the Trees and is looking  for tree makers  and sponsors  for that
  event.

  Mayor  Davila  asked Mr. Costley  to reach out to KIPP  Corazon.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked Mr. Costley  if tickets  are still  available  for the
  Brealdast  with  Santa event for December  13fh.

  Mr. Costley  responded  that there are some tickets  available.  There  are
  some dedicated  tickets  for commissions  and coiu'icil.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  stated that on November  ISt the South Gate Junior
  Athletic  Association  held their  fifth  annual  toy drive  in partnership  with
  the South  Gate Police  Department.  They  were able to get over 400 toys
  donated.  Two police  cruisers  were filled  up.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  stated that over hundred  players  participated  in a mini
  tournament.  He donated  championship  rings to the kids that participated.
  He mentioned  that each player,  parents  and businesses  donated  toys. A
  special  shoutout  to Javier  Zamora,  South  Gate resident,  that each year
  shows up with  a car full  of toys and Vice Mayor  Barron's  father,  who
  spends $1,000  dollars  on toys.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  promoted  the South  Gate Kiwanis'  monthly  cleanup
  event on Saturday,  November  15th starting  at 9:00 a.m.  Lastly,  November
  21s', the SELA  Kiwanis  is hosting  their  second  annual  Taste of SELA
  banquet  and asked to visit  their  Instagram  page at selakiwanis.org  to

2
CITY  COUNCIL

APPOINTMENTS  The City  Council  introduced  Ordinance  No. 2025-02-CC  entitled
  Ordinance  of the City  Council  of the City  of South  Gate, California,
  amending  Section  1.25.020  (Membership)  of Chapter  1.25 (Citizens'
  Advisory  Committee),  of Title  l (Administration  and Personnel),  of the
  South  Gate Municipal  Code to reduce  the number  of appointed  committee

  members  to ten (10) entitling  each Council  Member  to appoint  two (2)

  committee  members from among  qualified  residents  of the city who are
  eighteen  years of age or older. Before taking office, each committee
  member  shall be confirmed  by a majority  vote of the City Council during
  Consent  Calendar.
